body.statement:
For the exact-support witness graphs \(G_\star,H_\star\), row exchange and nonzero source rescaling give a bijection of their entire exact-support observational parameter spaces, without a centering or moment restriction, and therefore \(\mathcal P_{\{\varnothing\}}(G_\star)=\mathcal P_{\{\varnothing\}}(H_\star)\).  Every intervention family \(\mathcal I\) containing \(\{X_1\}\) separates them: \(\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(G_\star)
e\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(H_\star)\).  Indeed, under \(\operatorname{do}(X_1=z)\), every \(G_\star\) kernel makes \(X_2\) and \(X_3\) independent, whereas every \(H_\star\) kernel makes them dependent.  On the submodel whose source coordinates additionally have finite second moments, the corresponding covariances are \(0\) for \(G_\star\) and \(\gamma\delta\operatorname{Var}(\eta_L)
e0\) for arbitrary exact-support \(H_\star\) coefficients \(\gamma\) on \(L	o X_2\) and \(\delta\) on \(L	o X_3\); under the observational bijection this latter value is \(-(c/a)d\sigma_L^2
e0\).
body.justification: A uniform all-parameter witness proves that the interventional quotient is strictly finer than the observational quotient without relying on genericity.
body.gap: The zero-allowed version of this witness is false at zero pivots; the claim here is restricted to the newly specified exact nonzero support and re-proves the full parameter-space bijection directly.
body.consumer: The witness tells perturbation planners when one observed-node intervention resolves a feedback reversal and latent-parent ambiguity that no observational sample can resolve.
body.proof_tex:
By Definition \texttt{def:witness-mechanisms}, an arbitrary mechanism on \(G_\star\) has equations
\[
L=\varepsilon_L,\quad
X_1=cL+aX_2+\varepsilon_1,\quad
X_2=bX_1+\varepsilon_2,\quad
X_3=dL+\varepsilon_3.
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:exact-support} gives \(a,b,c,d\ne0\).  Since \(\varnothing\in\mathcal I\), Assumption \texttt{ass:regime-solvability} applied to the observational regime gives
\[
\det(I-B)=1-ab\ne0.
\]
Define coefficients and sources for \(H_\star\) by
\[
\alpha=b^{-1},\quad
\beta=a^{-1},\quad
\gamma=-ca^{-1},\quad
\delta=d,
\]
and
\[
\eta_L=\varepsilon_L,\quad
\eta_1=-b^{-1}\varepsilon_2,\quad
\eta_2=-a^{-1}\varepsilon_1,\quad
\eta_3=\varepsilon_3.
\]
All divisions are licensed by \(ab\ne0\).  A permutation followed by nonzero coordinatewise scaling preserves mutual independence and nonconstancy.  It also preserves non-Gaussianity: if \(rW\) were Gaussian for \(r\ne0\), then \(W=r^{-1}(rW)\) would be Gaussian.  Thus the source restrictions in Definition \texttt{def:exact-support-model-class} are preserved without using centering or moments.

The same endogenous vector satisfies the resulting \(H_\star\) equations sample by sample.  Indeed,
\[
\alpha X_2+\eta_1
=b^{-1}(X_2-\varepsilon_2)
=X_1
\]
by the \(G_\star\) equation for \(X_2\), while
\[
\gamma L+\beta X_1+\eta_2
=-ca^{-1}L+a^{-1}(X_1-\varepsilon_1)
=X_2
\]
by the \(G_\star\) equation for \(X_1\).  Also \(L=\eta_L\) and \(X_3=\delta L+\eta_3\).  Consequently the two observational vectors agree almost surely under this coupling and have the same law.

The transformed mechanism has exact support \(H_\star\), because \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta\ne0\).  Its feedback determinant is
\[
1-\alpha\beta
=1-\frac{1}{ab}
=\frac{ab-1}{ab}\ne0.
\]
For either witness graph and any observed intervention target \(S\), the only directed cycle remaining in the equations indexed by \(V\setminus S\) is the \(X_1,X_2\) two-cycle when \(S\cap\{X_1,X_2\}=\varnothing\).  Therefore
\[
\det(Q_{V\setminus S,V\setminus S})
=\begin{cases}
1-ab,&S\cap\{X_1,X_2\}=\varnothing\quad\text{for }G_\star,\\
1-\alpha\beta,&S\cap\{X_1,X_2\}=\varnothing\quad\text{for }H_\star,\\
1,&S\cap\{X_1,X_2\}\ne\varnothing.
\end{cases}
\]
Thus every required intervention system is invertible, and no stability restriction has been used.

Conversely, let an arbitrary admissible \(H_\star\) mechanism have nonzero coefficients \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta\) and mutually independent nonconstant non-Gaussian sources \(\eta\).  Its observational solvability gives \(1-\alpha\beta\ne0\).  Set
\[
a=\beta^{-1},\qquad
b=\alpha^{-1},\qquad
c=-\gamma\beta^{-1},\qquad
d=\delta,
\]
and
\[
\varepsilon_L=\eta_L,\quad
\varepsilon_1=-\beta^{-1}\eta_2,\quad
\varepsilon_2=-\alpha^{-1}\eta_1,\quad
\varepsilon_3=\eta_3.
\]
Then \(a,b,c,d\ne0\), the source restrictions are preserved by the same argument, and
\[
1-ab
=1-\frac{1}{\alpha\beta}
=\frac{\alpha\beta-1}{\alpha\beta}\ne0.
\]
Direct substitution shows that this construction is inverse to the preceding one on coefficients and source laws.  Hence it is a bijection of the complete exact-support observational mechanism spaces.  Definition \texttt{def:graph-law-set} now yields
\[
\mathcal P_{\{\varnothing\}}(G_\star)
=\mathcal P_{\{\varnothing\}}(H_\star).
\]

It remains to distinguish the joint intervention classes.  By Assumption \texttt{ass:perfect-intervention}, \(\operatorname{do}(X_1=z)\) replaces only the equation for \(X_1\).  For an arbitrary \(G_\star\) mechanism, the remaining relevant equations are
\[
X_2=bz+\varepsilon_2,
\qquad
X_3=d\varepsilon_L+\varepsilon_3.
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:source-independence} says that \(\varepsilon_2\) is independent of \((\varepsilon_L,\varepsilon_3)\).  Measurable transformations of independent random elements are independent, so \(X_2\) and \(X_3\) are independent in every such kernel.  This step uses neither centering nor moments.

For an arbitrary \(H_\star\) mechanism, write
\[
L=\eta_L,\quad
X_1=\alpha X_2+\eta_1,\quad
X_2=\gamma L+\beta X_1+\eta_2,\quad
X_3=\delta L+\eta_3.
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:exact-support} gives \(\gamma\delta\ne0\), and Assumption \texttt{ass:source-nondegeneracy} says that \(\eta_L\) is nonconstant.  Surgery at \(X_1=z\) gives
\[
X_2=\gamma\eta_L+\beta z+\eta_2,
\qquad
X_3=\delta\eta_L+\eta_3.
\]
Constants do not affect independence.  Apply Lemma \texttt{lem:single-shared-source-dependence} with
\[
U=\eta_L,\quad R_1=\eta_2,\quad R_2=\eta_3,\quad r=\gamma,\quad s=\delta.
\]
Its hypotheses follow from Assumptions \texttt{ass:source-independence}, \texttt{ass:source-nondegeneracy}, and \texttt{ass:exact-support}; hence \(X_2\) and \(X_3\) are dependent in every \(H_\star\) singleton-intervention kernel.

Independence of two coordinates is determined by their joint probability law.  Thus a \(G_\star\) kernel under \(\operatorname{do}(X_1=z)\) cannot equal an \(H_\star\) kernel under that intervention.  If \(\{X_1\}\in\mathcal I\), equality of two joint response-kernel tuples would imply equality of these singleton components, which is impossible.  Both graph model sets are nonempty: choose, for example, nonzero coefficients with feedback product different from one and mutually independent centered Laplace sources; the determinant calculation above verifies every observed intervention regime.  By Definitions \texttt{def:response-kernel-tuple} and \texttt{def:graph-law-set},
\[
\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(G_\star)
\ne
\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(H_\star)
\qquad\text{whenever }\{X_1\}\in\mathcal I.
\]

Finally, impose the finite-second-moment condition of Assumption \texttt{ass:source-second-moment} only for the covariance certificate.  Bilinearity of covariance and independence give, for \(G_\star\),
\[
\operatorname{Cov}(X_2,X_3)
=d\operatorname{Cov}(\varepsilon_2,\varepsilon_L)
+\operatorname{Cov}(\varepsilon_2,\varepsilon_3)
=0.
\]
For \(H_\star\), the same calculation gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Cov}(X_2,X_3)
&=\gamma\delta\operatorname{Var}(\eta_L)
+\gamma\operatorname{Cov}(\eta_L,\eta_3)
+\delta\operatorname{Cov}(\eta_2,\eta_L)
+\operatorname{Cov}(\eta_2,\eta_3)\\
&=\gamma\delta\operatorname{Var}(\eta_L).
\end{aligned}
\]
Finite second moment and nonconstancy imply \(\operatorname{Var}(\eta_L)>0\), while exact support gives \(\gamma\delta\ne0\); therefore the last display is nonzero.  Under the inverse parametrization, \(\gamma=-c/a\), \(\delta=d\), and \(\eta_L=\varepsilon_L\), so it equals
\[
-\frac{c}{a}d\sigma_L^2\ne0.
\]
This proves the conditional covariance clause.  The identification argument uses no treatment overlap or positivity condition because it compares perfect-intervention population kernels at fixed \(z\); it uses no boundary or limiting argument.
